```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

credgate removes personal data from text *before* it reaches a language
model. This vignette shows the workflow with models served locally by
[Ollama](https://ollama.com) or [vLLM](https://docs.vllm.ai), using
[ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org). All data is synthetic.

## Why redact when the model is local?

"Local" does not by itself make a workflow compliant:

- a vLLM server is often **shared** by several teams;
- prompts end up in **server logs** and request traces;
- a **RAG index** keeps every chunk it is given, PII included;
- **fine-tuning sets** built from chat logs carry PII forward;
- model **answers** copy PII into reports and tickets;
- the DPDP Act's **data minimisation** and purpose limitation apply wherever
  the model runs.

## 1. Preview, then redact

Always look at what will be sent first:

```{r}
library(credgate)

note <- paste(
  "Customer name: Priya Nair. Called about her home-loan EMI. PAN ABCPN1234K,",
  "mobile +91 98765 43210, UPI priya.n@oksbi. She wants the EMI date moved",
  "to the 10th because her salary is credited late."
)
preview(note, min_confidence = 0.5)
```

`redact()` returns the text that is safe to send; identifiers become
placeholders naming their type:

```{r}
safe <- redact(note, min_confidence = 0.5)
safe
```

`min_confidence = 0.5` leaves low-confidence matches alone (for example a
12-digit order number that happens to pass the Aadhaar checksum, scored 0.42
because of the word "order"). Use `0` to redact every match.

> **Check the preview.** Names are found next to an honorific, a relation or
> a field label (`Shri`, `S/o`, `Name:`, `नाम:`). A name in running text
> without such a cue - "Customer Priya Nair called" - is **not** detected
> yet, and would reach the model.

## 2. Ollama

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(ellmer)

chat <- chat_ollama(model = "gemma3:1b")
chat$chat(paste("Summarise this call note in one sentence:", safe, sep = "\n"))
```

The model only ever sees `[PERSON_NAME]`, `[PAN]`, `[MOBILE_IN]` and
`[UPI_ID]`.

## 3. vLLM (or any OpenAI-compatible server)

vLLM serves the OpenAI-compatible API. ellmer's `chat_vllm()` talks to it;
set `VLLM_API_KEY` if your server checks keys (local servers usually do not,
but ellmer requires a value).

```{r, eval = FALSE}
if (!nzchar(Sys.getenv("VLLM_API_KEY"))) Sys.setenv(VLLM_API_KEY = "unused")

tickets <- c(
  "Shri Ramesh Kumar (Aadhaar 5422 2937 1182) reports a failed UPI payment to ramesh@okaxis.",
  "Account 50100987654321, IFSC HDFC0004567: customer asks to update email to priya.nair@example.org."
)
chat <- chat_vllm(
  base_url = "http://localhost:8000/v1",
  model = "meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct",
  system_prompt = "Classify the ticket as PAYMENTS, PROFILE or GENERAL. Answer with one word."
)
for (ticket in tickets) {
  print(chat$clone()$chat(redact(ticket, min_confidence = 0.5)))
}
```

The same code works with Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint
(`base_url = "http://localhost:11434/v1"`), LM Studio, a llama.cpp server or
an internal gateway.

## 4. Getting the real values back: tokenise and restore

Redaction is one-way: the model's answer can only say `[PAN]`. When the
answer should name the customer - a drafted reply, a summary for a case
file - tokenise instead. Each identifier becomes a numbered token, the
vault remembers what it stands for, and `restore()` puts the values back:

```{r}
vault <- cg_vault()
safe <- tokenise(note, vault, min_confidence = 0.5)
safe
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
answer <- chat_ollama(model = "gemma3:1b")$chat(
  paste("Draft a two-line reply to this customer:", safe)
)
restore(answer, vault)
```

Without a model at hand, this is what `restore()` does with a typical
answer - including tokens the model copied loosely:

```{r}
restore("Dear [PERSON_NAME_1], we have noted PAN [ pan_1 ] and will call MOBILE_IN_1.", vault)
```

The same identifier always gets the same token, so the model can still tell
two customers apart. `restore(strict = TRUE)` stops if the answer contains
a token the vault does not know. The vault prints with values masked:

```{r}
vault
```

## 5. Data frames: find the PII, send only what is needed

```{r}
complaints <- data.frame(
  cust_pan = c("ABCPE1234F", "AAACR5055K", "XYZPQ9876R"),
  mobile = c(9876543210, 8826781145, 9123456780),
  complaint = c(
    "EMI debited twice from A/c 50100123456789; please refund.",
    "Shri Mohan Lal wants the statement sent to mohan.lal@example.com.",
    "App crashes when opening the cards tab."
  )
)
scan_pii(complaints)
```

Only the complaint text is needed to categorise complaints, so send only
that column, redacted:

```{r}
prompts <- paste("Categorise this complaint:", redact(complaints$complaint, min_confidence = 0.5))
prompts
```

## 6. Measure it on your own data

If you have labelled examples of your documents, `cg_evaluate()` reports
precision, recall and F1 per type, so you can decide on a threshold with
evidence:

```{r}
docs <- list(
  list(text = "PAN: ABCPE1234F", spans = list(list(start = 5, end = 15, type = "pan"))),
  list(text = "order no 878245671885", spans = list())
)
cg_evaluate(docs, min_confidence = 0.5)
```

## Limits and what comes next

- The vault behind `tokenise()` lives in memory: when the R session ends,
  the tokens can no longer be restored. Saving it, encrypted, is next.
- You call `redact()` or `tokenise()` yourself. A planned **proxy mode** - a local
  OpenAI-compatible server in front of Ollama or vLLM - will redact,
  restore and audit automatically, so tools you cannot change (Open WebUI,
  Continue, Positron, Jupyter AI) are covered by pointing their base URL at
  it.

Runnable versions of these examples, in R, Python and the shell, are in the
[`examples/`](https://github.com/dwarpal/credgate/tree/main/examples)
folder of the repository.
